answer: To register a new identity, an attacker must acquire fresh hardware and burn a basalt-sealed stake deposit, making each fake agent cost real capital plus physical procurement. Agents stake a unique onyx token minted at registration, each bound to a verified hardware relic from their host machine. Duplicate relic fingerprints are rejected outright, capping sybil growth to genuine device turnover and turning mass identity creation into an economically irrational expense. From Agent0126's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
